To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FLS isolated from the inflamed joints of K/BxN transgenic mice express a proinflammatory phenotype and are responsive to both TNF-α and glucocorticoid signalling.

fibroblast-like cells isolated from K/BXN mice are a good model of human rheumatoid arthritis synovial fibroblasts and that they respond in a similar manner to pro- and antiinflammatory cytokines as human fibroblast-like cell populations.

FLS isolated from a murine inflammatory model possess significantly elevated expression of inflammatory genes, which is enhanced in the presence TNF-α and abrogated by corticosterone, and can be used to assess novel therapeutics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of fibroblast like synoviocytes (FSLs) in the pathogenesis of inflammatory joint diseases, and the development of novel therapies for these diseases.
the identification of the key molecular mechanisms which drive the development and progression of joint inflammation.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies in inflammatory arthritis, and this model provides a useful tool in the development of such therapies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FLS from the K/BxN mouse model of inflammatory joint disease are an appropriate model for the study of inflammatory joint diseases.
FLS isolated from the K/BxN model are a useful tool for in vitro studies of joint inflammation.
the K/BxN murine FLS is a suitable model to study the inflammatory environment of the synovium in inflammatory arthritis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have established a well characterized murine FLS model that will allow the identification of novel targets for therapeutic intervention in inflammatory joint disease.
this study has provided a well-characterised murine model for the study of fibroblast like synoviocyte (FLS) biology.
this study provides a well characterised model for FLS culture and inflammatory signalling in the K/BxN model of inflammatory arthritis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FLS from inflamed joints are more responsive to TNF-α and express more inflammatory genes than FLS from non-inflammed joints.
we have developed a well-characterised set of key inflammation-related genes for in vitro murine fibroblast-like-synoviocyte (FLS) culture.
we have developed a model system to study the role of fibroblast like synoviocytes in joint inflammation and that the K/BxN mouse strain provides a good model for this.
